reason: Conversation 2 ran a sensible water test, correctly interpreted H98 as a magnetron/inverter high-voltage fault once the full model was known, gave consistent casing-off safety warnings and escalated to an engineer; its only flaw was leaning slightly hard on 'most common cause is the inverter board' without an engineer confirming. Conversation 1 never recognised what H98 means, kept calling the appliance a 'Panasonic NNH98' after the customer gave the real model, wasted turns on power-level and vent checks that the symptoms already ruled out, and gave an empty non-answer to the repair-worth question despite the customer volunteering the £300 price point. Both kept the homeowner safe, but 2 gave an honest, correct diagnosis while 1 was vague and partly wrong.
